inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 tanshin consolidated cash-flow statement, 'Share-based payment transactions' 384 (2801.T_Annual_FY2026.txt:908: 334 + 49 across the two equity movements; CSV StockBasedComp FY2026 = 384). EquityAwardTaxes = 0 (BIP Trust settles in shares; no net-share-settlement tax line). Filing units are JPY millions, same as the CSV.
inputs.share_count_basis: 969,416,010 issued less 42,872,742 treasury (incl. 898,714 BIP Trust shares) at 30 June 2026 = 926.543m, post 5:1 split of 1 April 2024. FY2026 tanshin line 1127: 'Diluted EPS is not shown because there are no dilutive potential common stocks', so basic = fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC (0.05% of revenue) is expensed in the flows; the FY2027 buyback programme (up to 24m shares / JPY30bn, May 2026-Mar 2027; nil executed by 30 June 2026) is the cash mechanism that funds the flat count and is value-neutral here.
inputs.wacc_rationale: JPY-denominated flows discounted at a JPY-built rate: 10y JGB ~1.7% risk-free + beta 0.8 x 6.0% Japan ERP = 6.5% cost of equity; borrowings are JPY18bn against JPY93bn cash so WACC = cost of equity = 6.5%. Below the ~9% house reference for keiretsu cyclicals because this is a low-beta global consumer staple with net cash; FX-translation risk (78% of revenue, ~90% of business profit earned in USD/EUR and reported in JPY) is charged in the scenario flows (bear = yen appreciation), NOT as a WACC premium, and the same WACC is used in all three scenarios (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. IFRS 16 filer: lease liabilities JPY43,585m (Q1 FY2027) are EXCLUDED from net debt; total_debt is borrowings only (4,003 current + 14,000 long-term). The full lease payment (principal JPY8,170m FY2026 + estimated lease interest ~JPY1,100m, ~2.5% on the liability; the tanshin does not split lease interest out of 'interest paid' 1,842) is charged inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path at 1.25% of revenue. D&A for cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation: total D&A 26,746 (3.6% of revenue) less ROU depreciation estimated at ~8.2bn (approximately equal to principal repayments; ROU assets 38.3bn) = ~18.5bn = 2.5% of revenue, ramping to 2.8% as the Jefferson plant depreciates. last_fcf deducts the FY2026 lease principal so the FY0 owner-FCF base is on the same footing as the forward build.
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated flows; non-controlling interests deducted once in the equity bridge at book (JPY8,043m, Q1 FY2027). NCI profit share is ~JPY0.8bn/yr (~1.2% of group profit); valuing it at the group's implied multiple instead of book would move the result by under JPY10/share.
inputs.matching_assets_note: Interest AND dividend income are stripped from the flows (the FY2026 'Interest and dividend income' line is JPY4,637m: ~3,142 interest + 1,495 dividends received). Their source assets go into the bridge once: cash JPY93,230m via net debt, and non-current 'Other financial assets' JPY80,497m (Q1 FY2027; the FVOCI equity portfolio sits here, FY2026 FVOCI fair-value gain +7,165; 1,495/80,497 = 1.9% dividend yield is consistent with a listed Japanese cross-shareholding book) via equity_bridge. Current other financial assets JPY27,734m (time deposits/short-term securities) are left OUT of the bridge as a conservatism; including them would add ~JPY30/share.
inputs.capex_definition: reported_fcf (CSV FreeCashFlow 34,116) is OCF 90,508 less purchase of PP&E 56,392 only; FY2026 intangibles purchases of 3,220 are not in it. The forward capex_pct_path covers PP&E + intangibles (FY2026 59,612 = 8.0% of revenue, FY2025 40,669 = 5.7%, FY2024 29,702 = 4.5%, FY2019-FY2023 average ~4.5%). FY2026-FY2027 is the peak of the Jefferson, Wisconsin plant build (opened fall 2026); capex glides back to ~4% of revenue by FY2033.
inputs.working_capital_note: Manufacturer + wholesale distributor: trade receivables 90,640 + inventories 110,358 - trade payables 72,002 = 128,996 net working capital = 17.3% of FY2026 revenue. Growth consumes cash, so wc_capture_pct is NEGATIVE at -15% of the YoY revenue change (slightly below the balance-sheet ratio because payables have grown faster than receivables in FY2025-FY2026).
inputs.tax_note: FY2026 income taxes 21,910 on profit before tax 84,069 = 26.1% P&L rate; cash taxes paid 18,946 = 22.5% (timing; FY2025 cash rate was 26.1%). Japan statutory ~30.6%, US federal+state ~25%; ~90% of business profit is overseas. 26% cash tax rate held flat across the horizon.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, non-US), routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'Operating company, non-US' with owner-fcf-adaptations.md applied: (a1) JPY WACC, (b) one lease treatment (B), (c) NCI charged once in the bridge, (d) stripped interest+dividend income matched by cash and the non-current financial-asset portfolio in the bridge, (e) SBC near-zero (0.05% of revenue, so house and street nearly coincide), (f) risk charged once, in the flows. Fresh build (no prior DCF or memory entry). FY0 = FY2026 (year ended 31 March 2026); anchors: price 2026-10-26, balance sheet and share count from the Q1 FY2027 tanshin (30 June 2026). Reported in JPY and quoted in JPY; no FX conversion of outputs. FX context: USDJPY 156.9 on 2026-10-26 (Yahoo JPY=X) vs the FY2027 guidance assumption of 155 and FY2026 average 150.97, so the current rate is a mild tailwind to guidance; a reversion toward 140 is the bear axis. Owner-FCF FY2026 base = 34,116 - 384 SBC - 4,637 interest and dividend income - 8,170 lease principal = 20,925 (2.8% of revenue), depressed by peak plant capex. Horizon 10 years because capex is still normalising and margins still ramping at year 5.

equity_bridge.item: Non-current other financial assets (FVOCI equity portfolio and long-term financial assets) at carrying/fair value
equity_bridge.note: Q1 FY2027 tanshin balance sheet (2801.T_Quarterly_Q1-FY2027.txt:475). Matches the stripped dividend income (1,495) and the portion of interest income not earned on cash.
Q1 FY2027 tanshin balance sheet line 519; consolidated flows, so NCI is deducted once here.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Medium-Term Management Plan FY2026-FY2028 target of >5%/yr sales growth ex-FX, cross-checked against the 6.4% 3yr revenue CAGR. The equity and EPS CAGRs (11-15%) are not used as the growth anchor because roughly half of the 5yr revenue CAGR is yen depreciation (USDJPY ~106 in FY2021 to ~151 in FY2026) translated into JPY, which does not repeat.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 11.0% diverges >30% from revenue 3yr CAGR 6.4%. Cause: FX translation reserve gains on overseas net assets plus a ~38% payout ratio retaining most earnings. Not treated as a signal of underlying growth.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC, interest+dividend income and IFRS 16 lease principal): FY2021 34,889; FY2022 26,631; FY2023 24,650; FY2024 39,445; FY2025 19,904; FY2026 20,925. Owner-FCF CAGRs are negative (-5.3% 3yr, -9.7% 5yr) while reported FCF is ~flat: the gap is NOT SBC (negligible) but (i) interest income rising from 1.1bn to 4.6-6.5bn as USD rates rose, which is cash-pile income not operating value, and (ii) lease principal rising from 5.4bn to 8.2bn. Both series are depressed in FY2025-FY2026 by the Jefferson plant capex supercycle (capex 5.7% and 8.0% of revenue vs ~4.5% normal); FCF CAGRs are therefore not used to set growth.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 7.5% vs guidance 7.2% (Q1 FY2027 ran +15.0% and USDJPY 157 vs the 155 assumption); then decays from the MTP's >5% ex-FX toward 2.5% nominal JPY growth by FY2035. Post-IFRS16 EBITDA margin has sat in a 12.5-14.2% band FY2022-FY2026 (13.8% FY2026); base lets Jefferson operating leverage and manufacturing mix add 70bp over seven years. Capex normalises from the 7-8% plant peak to 4% by FY2033.

scenario_narratives.base: Kikkoman delivers roughly its FY2027 guidance (revenue +7.2%, business profit +3.5% at USDJPY 155) with Q1's +15% start fading as comps normalise, then grows at the MTP's ~5% ex-FX pace with the yen broadly stable, decaying to 2.5% nominal by the mid-2030s. The Jefferson, Wisconsin plant ramps through FY2027-FY2029, taking capex from 8% of revenue back to ~4% and adding ~70bp of EBITDA margin via manufacturing mix (the ~7%-margin Overseas Wholesale segment still grows but the ~20%+ margin North American manufacturing grows faster). Working capital absorbs ~15% of each year's revenue increase as receivables and inventory scale with the distribution business. Terminal value is bounded at 20x owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: North American soy sauce and seasoning demand absorbs the new capacity faster than planned, Europe and ASEAN deliver the targeted double-digit growth, and the yen stays at or weaker than 155, so JPY revenue compounds at 7-10% for three years and 5%+ through FY2032. Operating leverage on the fixed-cost plant base plus pricing lifts post-IFRS16 EBITDA margin to 16% (operating margin ~12%, above the MTP's 10% floor), the balance sheet keeps funding JPY20-30bn/yr of buybacks, and the group earns the 12%+ ROE target. Terminal growth 2.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The yen reverts toward 140/USD during FY2028, erasing ~8% of translated overseas revenue and business profit (78% of revenue, ~90% of profit is non-yen), while US food-service volumes soften and raw-material and freight costs (Middle East-related, flagged as unmodelled in guidance) compress margins. Post-IFRS16 EBITDA margin slips to 12.5%, growth in JPY terms is ~2%, and the Jefferson plant is a fixed cost on a smaller translated revenue base, so capex stays at 4.5% of revenue. The domestic business continues to rely on price not volume. No solvency axis: net cash and an 11.5% D/E ratio keep the bear case a slower, lower-margin compounder, not a distressed one. Terminal multiple capped at 16x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bull weight is cut because the bull case needs three independent things to hold at once: a yen that stays near 20-year lows, a clean Jefferson ramp, and 200bp of margin expansion the company has never sustained under IFRS. Bear weight is raised to 25% because the single largest axis, yen appreciation, is a mean-reversion risk that has nothing to do with execution and which management itself flags; there is no going-concern or covenant dimension, so bear does not go higher than 25%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Kikkoman is a genuine franchise: the default soy sauce brand outside Asia, locally brewed in the US since 1973, a defensive staple with net cash and rising capital returns. The owner-FCF model nonetheless values it well below the market because (i) the Wholesale segment that generates 58% of revenue ties up ~17% of revenue in working capital, so growth consumes cash, (ii) FY2025-FY2027 free cash flow is depressed by the ~$560m Jefferson plant, and (iii) at a 28x trailing P/E the market is capitalising JPY earnings that include roughly half a decade of yen depreciation. The gap between house value and price is mostly the multiple the market pays for the brand's durability and FX-translated earnings, which a JPY-based owner-FCF model does not grant. This is a quality compounder at a growth-stock price; the valuation says wait for either a stronger yen or a de-rating.
key_risks_to_valuation: FX translation: a 10% yen appreciation removes ~8% of JPY revenue and ~9% of business profit in the year it happens; the FY2027 guidance is struck at 155 and USDJPY is 157 today.

Working-capital assumption: wc_capture -15% is the single largest drag on owner FCF relative to EBITDA; if payables keep growing faster than receivables (as in FY2026) the true capture could be nearer -10%, worth a meaningful uplift to IV.

Lease split estimates: lease interest (~1.1bn) and ROU depreciation (~8.2bn) are estimated from the liability and principal repayments because the tanshin does not disclose them; the yuho would refine both, with limited per-share effect.

Terminal cap: Gordon at 6.5%/2.0% is 22.7x so the 20x cap binds in base and bull; a buyer paying today's ~28x earnings multiple for the terminal business is the re-rating the model deliberately does not assume.
Equity portfolio: JPY80.5bn of non-current other financial assets is added at carrying value without a disclosed split between listed equities and other items; a 25% haircut would cost ~JPY22/share.
Capex normalisation: the model assumes the plant build is a cycle, returning capex to ~4% of revenue; a second overseas capacity programme (Europe, ASEAN) would extend the 5-7% phase.
